tasks.title: Implement the LIST setting kind (ListSpec) with definition and value validation
tasks.red_command: uv run pytest tests/acceptance/settings_coverage/ tests/unit/test_settings_coverage.py tests/property/test_settings_coverage.py tests/contract/settings_coverage/ -v
implementation_steps: Add LIST to the SettingKind enum in src/backend/settings/models.py (the 7th kind)
Create the ListSpec frozen Pydantic model in src/backend/settings/models.py: item_pattern (str | None), min_items (int | None), max_items (int | None), allow_duplicates (bool, default True)

Add an optional list_spec: ListSpec | None field to SettingDefinition, validated exactly like the existing slider_spec / select_spec: LIST requires a valid ListSpec (present or the default ListSpec()); non-LIST kinds reject a ListSpec; a ListSpec is invalid when min_items > max_items, item_pattern is not a valid regex, or min_items/max_items is negative

Implement LIST value validation in the registry's per-kind validation: the value is a list of strings; each item fullmatches item_pattern (when set); the item count is within [min_items, max_items] (when set); duplicates are rejected when allow_duplicates is False; invalid values raise SettingsValidationError
Map any pydantic.ValidationError raised during LIST construction/validation to SettingsValidationError so the public error contract is the SettingsError hierarchy
Export ListSpec and the LIST kind from src/backend/settings/__init__.py
tasks.green_command: uv run pytest tests/acceptance/settings_coverage/ tests/unit/test_settings_coverage.py tests/property/test_settings_coverage.py tests/contract/settings_coverage/ -v
design_constraints: ListSpec is a frozen Pydantic model
LIST requires a valid ListSpec; non-LIST kinds reject a ListSpec
LIST value validation: list of strings, per-item fullmatch, count bounds, duplicate control
Construction/validation errors raise SettingsValidationError (never pydantic.ValidationError)
completion_gates: Acceptance tests for AC-007 through AC-012 pass
Edge tests for EDGE-005, EDGE-006, EDGE-012 pass

tasks.title: Implement value persistence (ValueRepository + YamlValueRepository + registry persistence)
tasks.red_command: uv run pytest tests/acceptance/settings_coverage/ tests/unit/test_settings_coverage.py tests/property/test_settings_coverage.py tests/contract/settings_coverage/ -v
implementation_steps: Create the ValueRepository ABC in src/backend/settings/repository.py with load() -> dict[str, Any] | None and save(values: dict[str, Any]) -> None

Implement YamlValueRepository(directory): a single values.yaml file (safe YAML); write atomically (write to a temp file in the same directory and rename over the target) so the file is always absent or valid YAML; thread-safe; directory created if missing
Implement YamlValueRepository.load(): return None for a missing file; raise ValueStorageError for corrupted or schema-invalid content
Add a value_repository: ValueRepository | None = None constructor parameter to SettingsRegistry; when None, use a default YamlValueRepository('settings')

Implement registry value persistence: load persisted values at construction and apply them to the settings (persisted > default); persist all current values on every change (set_value, reset, reset_all, template loads)
Add ValueStorageError to the SettingsError hierarchy in src/backend/settings/exceptions.py
Ensure the settings feature registers no settings of its own (it is the source of truth; its persistence directory is a constructor parameter, default 'settings')
tasks.green_command: uv run pytest tests/acceptance/settings_coverage/ tests/unit/test_settings_coverage.py tests/property/test_settings_coverage.py tests/contract/settings_coverage/ -v
design_constraints: ValueRepository is the stable storage interface (load/save)
A values.yaml file is always either absent or valid YAML (atomic writes)
load returns None for missing, raises ValueStorageError for corrupted
Persisted values take precedence over definition defaults (persisted > default)
All current values are persisted (including those equal to their default)
The settings feature registers no settings of its own

Edge tests for EDGE-003, EDGE-004, EDGE-009 pass
Property tests for INV-002, INV-005 pass
Contract tests for NFR-005 pass

tasks.title: Resolve the EventBus bootstrapping cycle with a guarded read
tasks.red_command: uv run pytest tests/acceptance/settings_coverage/ tests/unit/test_settings_coverage.py tests/property/test_settings_coverage.py tests/contract/settings_coverage/ -v
implementation_steps: In the EventBus constructor (src/backend/eventbus/), use the guarded read get_settings_registry(required=False)
If the registry already exists (the guarded read is not None), read eventbus.max_queue_size from the registry
Otherwise (the registry does not exist yet), use the hardcoded default 1000
Ensure no infinite recursion occurs when the registry's default event bus is created during the first get_settings_registry()
tasks.green_command: uv run pytest tests/acceptance/settings_coverage/ tests/unit/test_settings_coverage.py tests/property/test_settings_coverage.py tests/contract/settings_coverage/ -v
design_constraints: The EventBus constructor uses the guarded read (no side effect)
The first EventBus (created during the first get_settings_registry()) uses the hardcoded default 1000
A later EventBus (created after the registry exists) reads eventbus.max_queue_size from the registry
No infinite recursion

Edge test for EDGE-001 passes

tasks.title: Implement feature-owned registration, live reads, and constructor defaults (all 4 features)

implementation_steps: Add a register_settings(registry) function to each feature module (src/backend/logging/, src/backend/authentication/, src/backend/usermanagement/, src/backend/eventbus/) that registers the feature's SettingDefinitions with the given registry (no import side effects)

Use the full feature name as the key prefix (logging.*, authentication.*, usermanagement.*, eventbus.*) and category = domain (application/security), group = feature name, per the inventory in section 3.5
Implement live reads: each feature reads its settings from the registry (get_value on each use) so a set_value affects a running feature without re-construction
Retain existing feature constructor parameters for DI/testing; their default becomes the registry value, and an explicit argument wins over the registry value
Implement the unregistered-key fallback: reading an unregistered key returns the feature's original hardcoded default and logs a warning
Convert time-based settings (session_ttl, reset_token_ttl, lockout_duration) from NUMBER seconds to timedelta at read time
Use the LIST kind for usermanagement.roles (item_pattern ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$, min_items 1)

Keys use the full feature name as the prefix; category = domain, group = feature name
